_README: Pre-defined incentive records keyed by source.key. Used by extractors/static_extractor.py to bypass LLM and bot-blocked sites for stable, well-documented programs. Add/edit entries directly. Each record matches the IncentiveRecord schema (program_name, state, city, incentive_type, property_type, description, eligibility_criteria, incentive_amount, valid_until, updated_at, review_needed, program_links). state/city are overwritten by the pipeline's region-stamp pass — leave 'Florida'/'Tampa' as defaults.

my_safe_fl_home.description: Florida-administered hurricane mitigation grant for owner-occupied single-family homes. Provides a free wind mitigation home inspection plus a matching grant (state pays $2 for every $1 the homeowner contributes) for approved improvements like roof reinforcement, opening protection (impact windows/shutters), and roof-to-wall connections. Funded by the Florida Legislature; managed by the Department of Financial Services.
my_safe_fl_home.eligibility_criteria: Owner-occupied single-family home in Florida with insured value under $700,000. Homeowner must have a homestead exemption. Property must be located in the wind-borne debris region. The home must be built before 2008 to qualify for the grant.
my_safe_fl_home.incentive_amount: Up to $10,000 grant (2:1 state match — homeowner contributes $1 for every $2 the state provides). Free home inspection valued at ~$150.

teco_rebates.program_name: TECO Residential Energy-Efficient Heat Pump Rebate
teco_rebates.description: Tampa Electric (TECO) rebate for installing a qualifying high-efficiency heat pump (≥15 SEER2 / 8.8 HSPF2). Available to TECO residential electric customers in Hillsborough, Pasco, Pinellas, and Polk counties.
teco_rebates.eligibility_criteria: TECO residential electric customer with permanent home in TECO service territory. Equipment must be installed by a TECO-participating contractor and meet minimum efficiency requirements. Existing system must be replaced (not new construction).
teco_rebates.incentive_amount: Up to $200 rebate per qualifying unit

teco_rebates.program_name: TECO Residential Insulation & Window Sun Screen Rebate
teco_rebates.description: Rebates for upgrading attic/wall insulation to recommended R-values and for installing solar window screens. Helps reduce summer cooling load in Tampa Bay homes.
teco_rebates.eligibility_criteria: TECO residential customer; pre-installation home energy survey may be required. Must use approved materials and pass post-installation inspection.
teco_rebates.incentive_amount: Insulation: variable based on R-value upgrade and square footage. Window sun screen: variable.

duke_fl_rebates.program_name: Duke Energy Florida Residential HVAC Rebate
duke_fl_rebates.description: Rebates for installing high-efficiency central air conditioners and heat pumps in Duke Energy Florida residential service territory (parts of Pinellas, Pasco, Citrus, Hernando, and other counties).
duke_fl_rebates.eligibility_criteria: Duke Energy Florida residential electric customer. Equipment must meet minimum SEER2/HSPF2 efficiency thresholds and be installed by a Duke-participating contractor.
duke_fl_rebates.incentive_amount: Variable — up to $250 per qualifying unit depending on efficiency tier

fl_housing.program_name: Florida Hometown Heroes Down Payment Assistance
fl_housing.description: Florida Housing Finance Corporation program providing forgivable down-payment and closing-cost assistance to qualified frontline workers and other income-eligible homebuyers. Pairs with a 30-year fixed-rate first mortgage.
fl_housing.eligibility_criteria: Must be a first-time homebuyer (haven't owned a home in the last 3 years). Income at or below 150% of AMI. Property must be primary residence in Florida. Borrower must complete a homebuyer education course and have a minimum FICO score (typically 640+).
fl_housing.incentive_amount: Up to 5% of the first mortgage amount, with a maximum of $35,000 in down payment / closing-cost assistance

fl_housing.program_name: Florida SHIP — State Housing Initiatives Partnership
fl_housing.description: State-funded affordable-housing program distributed through every Florida city/county. Local jurisdictions use SHIP dollars for down-payment assistance, owner-occupied home rehabilitation, disaster relief, and homeownership counseling.
fl_housing.eligibility_criteria: Income-qualified Florida residents (typically ≤80% AMI for Very Low / Low Income, ≤120% AMI for Moderate). Must apply through the local jurisdiction (city or county). Property must be primary residence.
fl_housing.incentive_amount: Varies by jurisdiction — typically $7,500–$50,000 in down-payment / rehab assistance

hillsborough_housing.program_name: Hillsborough County SHIP — Down Payment Assistance
hillsborough_housing.description: Hillsborough County's local administration of the Florida SHIP program. Provides down-payment and closing-cost assistance as a deferred-payment second mortgage to income-qualified first-time buyers purchasing in unincorporated Hillsborough County.
hillsborough_housing.eligibility_criteria: First-time homebuyer (no ownership in past 3 years). Income at or below 80% of AMI. Property in unincorporated Hillsborough County, owner-occupied as primary residence. Must complete county-approved homebuyer education.
hillsborough_housing.incentive_amount: Up to $50,000 deferred second mortgage (forgivable after a residency period; consult HCFL for current terms)

hillsborough_housing.description: Hillsborough County housing-rehabilitation program funded through SHIP and CDBG. Provides repair / code-compliance assistance for owner-occupied homes — roofs, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, accessibility modifications.
hillsborough_housing.eligibility_criteria: Owner-occupied primary residence in unincorporated Hillsborough County. Income at or below 80% of AMI. Must be current on property taxes and insurance. Home must require structural / code-compliance repairs.
hillsborough_housing.incentive_amount: Up to $50,000 in rehabilitation assistance (deferred-payment loan)

city_tampa_dev.program_name: City of Tampa Owner-Occupied Housing Rehabilitation Program
city_tampa_dev.description: City of Tampa Housing & Community Development program providing forgivable loans to income-qualified homeowners for major home repairs — roof replacement, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, code violations, and accessibility modifications.
city_tampa_dev.eligibility_criteria: Must own and occupy the home as primary residence within Tampa city limits. Household income at or below 80% of AMI. Must be current on mortgage, property taxes, and insurance. Home must be in need of substantial repairs.
city_tampa_dev.incentive_amount: Up to $50,000 forgivable loan (forgiven after 10–15 years of continued owner-occupancy)

city_tampa_dev.program_name: City of Tampa Down Payment Assistance
city_tampa_dev.description: City of Tampa down-payment and closing-cost assistance for income-qualified first-time homebuyers purchasing within Tampa city limits.
city_tampa_dev.eligibility_criteria: First-time homebuyer (no ownership in past 3 years). Household income at or below 80% of AMI. Property must be in Tampa city limits, owner-occupied. Must complete a HUD-approved homebuyer education course.

fema_mitigation.description: Federal post-disaster mitigation funding distributed through the state after a Presidential disaster declaration. Pays for projects that reduce future disaster damage — wind retrofits, elevation, flood-proofing, acquisition of repetitive-loss properties.
fema_mitigation.eligibility_criteria: Property in a state with an active Presidentially-declared disaster. Application is made through the State Hazard Mitigation Officer (Florida Division of Emergency Management). Project must demonstrate cost-effectiveness via FEMA's BCA tool. Typically 75% federal / 25% non-federal cost share.
fema_mitigation.incentive_amount: Variable — funded as a 75/25 federal/non-federal cost share. No fixed per-property cap.

fema_mitigation.description: FEMA's pre-disaster competitive grant program for hazard-mitigation projects. Funds capability-building, mitigation projects (including wind/flood retrofits), and codes/standards adoption — applied for through the state.
fema_mitigation.eligibility_criteria: Subapplicants must be local governments or eligible non-profits in a state that submits the prime application. Individual homeowners apply through their county or municipality. Typically 75% federal / 25% non-federal cost share (90/10 for small-impoverished communities).
fema_mitigation.incentive_amount: Variable — 75% federal cost share. No fixed per-property cap.

doe_weatherization.description: Federally funded program (DOE) administered in Florida by the Department of Economic Opportunity through local providers. Provides free energy-efficiency improvements — insulation, air sealing, HVAC tune-up/replacement, water-heater wraps, LED lighting — for income-qualified households.
doe_weatherization.eligibility_criteria: Household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level (or recipient of SSI/TANF). Owner-occupied or renter (with landlord consent). Apply through local Community Action Agency.
doe_weatherization.incentive_amount: No cash to homeowner — services delivered. Average DOE cost per home is ~$8,000 in materials and labor; in Florida, supplemented by LIHEAP funds.

rewiring_ira.program_name: IRA Home Energy Rebates — HOMES (HOMES Rebate Program)
rewiring_ira.description: Inflation Reduction Act (Section 50121) whole-home efficiency rebate program. Funded by DOE, administered state-by-state. Pays homeowners (and property owners of multifamily buildings) for retrofits that reduce modeled or measured energy use.
rewiring_ira.eligibility_criteria: Single-family or multifamily property in a state with an active HOMES program. Rebate amount depends on modeled or measured energy savings (≥20% qualifies; ≥35% qualifies for higher tier) and household income (low/moderate income households receive higher rebates).
rewiring_ira.incentive_amount: Up to $8,000 per single-family home for low-/moderate-income households achieving ≥35% modeled energy savings (lower tiers for smaller savings or higher incomes)

rewiring_ira.program_name: IRA Home Energy Rebates — HEAR (Home Electrification & Appliance Rebates)
rewiring_ira.description: Inflation Reduction Act (Section 50122) point-of-sale rebate for low- and moderate-income households purchasing qualified high-efficiency electric appliances and equipment — heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, induction ranges, electric panel upgrades, insulation/air sealing, and electric wiring.
rewiring_ira.eligibility_criteria: Household income at or below 150% of the AMI. Equipment must be ENERGY STAR certified (where applicable). Rebate is delivered at point of sale through participating contractors/retailers.
rewiring_ira.incentive_amount: Up to $14,000 per household total: heat pump (up to $8,000), heat-pump water heater ($1,750), heat-pump clothes dryer ($840), electric stove/cooktop/range/oven ($840), electric panel upgrade ($4,000), insulation/air sealing ($1,600), electric wiring ($2,500). 100% covered for ≤80% AMI; 50% for 80–150% AMI.

ygrene_pace.program_name: Florida PACE (Property Assessed Clean Energy) Financing
ygrene_pace.description: Property Assessed Clean Energy financing for residential energy-efficiency, solar, hurricane resilience (impact windows, roof), and water-conservation upgrades. Repayment is added to the property tax bill over 5–30 years; the lien transfers with the property. Multiple PACE administrators operate in Florida (Florida PACE Funding Agency, RenewPACE, FRED).
ygrene_pace.eligibility_criteria: Property owner of single-family residential property in a Florida county/city that has authorized PACE. Must be current on property taxes and mortgage. No FICO minimum; underwriting based on home equity and tax-payment history. Mortgage lender notification typically required.
ygrene_pace.incentive_amount: Project-based — typically up to 20% of the home's market value with no fixed cap. 100% financing with no money down.
